events.name: Spotlight: SIENNA SPIRO +
events.description:
+ American Express® Card Members can purchase tickets from Thu 8/27 10:30AM through Sat 8/29 11AM.

The Grammy Museum is thrilled to welcome rising artist SIENNA SPIRO for an evening discussing the release of her debut album, Visitor, her creative process, and more, with a special performance in the Museum's intimate 200-seat Clive Davis Theater.
A show-stopping vocal talent with uncompromising vision, SIENNA SPIRO transforms her most privately felt pain into something communal and cathartic. Since the fall 2025 debut of her global breakout hit “Die On This Hill,” the 20-year-old has stunned virtually everyone who’s heard her with songs that trace the ephemeral nature of love, setting her breathtaking voice against an elegant collision of soul and symphonic pop. While the London-born singer/songwriter has been making music since age 10, her arrival has been sudden and indelible. In a few short months, SIENNA: sold out her first North American headline tour within seconds; was shortlisted for the BRIT Awards’ coveted Critics’ Choice Award; starred and sang in a major Gap holiday campaign; performed an unforgettable rendition of her Platinum single “Die On This Hill” on “The Tonight Show,” and garnered critical acclaim from Rolling Stone, LA Times, NYLON, V Magazine, The New York Times and more while Variety hailed her “one of the greatest voices of her generation.”
By early 2026, in a testament to the enthralling power of her timeless songcraft and stunning voice, SIENNA lodged all three of her singles on the Billboard Hot 100 simultaneously with “You Stole The Show” and “The Visitor”  joining “Die On This Hill” — all before the release of her debut album. That changes with Visitor, a disarmingly candid and staggeringly beautiful LP out now via Capitol Records, that finds Sienna working with an elite lineup of producers and orchestral composers in legendary studios like New York City’s Electric Lady, London’s Abbey Road, and LA’s Valentine to give life to an ambitious yet viscerally felt concept. Equal parts soul-searching confession and existential inquiry, the album explores the inherent fragility of life and love, and SIENNA’s own journey as someone so “fearful of things ending and people leaving” that she’s often avoided new relationships or situations. “I’ve spent most of my life feeling like a visitor,” she says, “someone who’s just passing through.” But if the early days of her spectacular career have shown us anything, it’s that SIENNA SPIRO is here to stay. Released to widespread praise, Variety called Visitor “a collection rich in heartache and high points,” adding, “When a woman who sounds like she could huff and puff and blow all our houses down confesses to multiple layers of vulnerability, we stop and pay attention.” Rolling Stone deemed “Mono No Aware” a “Song you Need To Know” and wrote that SIENNA “showed up to sing [with] an intensity that shows how emotionally invested she is in the stories she’s sharing.” SPIN added “[SPIRO’s] music is autobiographical, emotionally charged, and arranged in a way that feels like it’s from a bygone era,” while Vogue dubbed her a “timeless talent … one of the most in-demand new names in music.”  SIENNA embarks on her sold out global “My House” headline tour this fall.
